description: The >>IF / >>ELSE / >>END-IF conditional-compilation directive (ISO §2023:7.3.16) - it selects source lines on a §2023:7.3.8 constant conditional expression. The three words are ONE construct (a >>ELSE outside a >>IF is not a directive), so they share a row. Implemented by ConditionalCompilationProcessor; the introduction gate rejects the directive words below 2002. The §2023:7.3 compiler-directive facility is a COBOL-2002 introduction: COBOL-85 has no compiler directives at all, so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source. The edition edge below 2023 is DERIVED, not quoted (VCR Table 7's discipline, rows 7.19/7.20 - the repo holds no 2002 or 2014 text, ratified decision #1): the derivation is (a) the M2 post-85 feature catalog in docs/ISO2023_CONFORMANCE_PLAN.md, which places '*>' inline comments, >>SOURCE FORMAT, conditional compilation and 'recognize-and-ignore of the other standard >> directives' in COBOL-2002, (b) the sibling row leap-second-directive-2002, already landed on the same derivation (kb/Work PB65), and (c) Annex E, which itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and does NOT list this directive among the additions, so it predates 2023. Overturnable in one line if the 2002/2014 text is ever acquired.
citation: ISO §2023:7.3.16; the §2023:7.3 compiler-directive facility is a COBOL-2002 introduction (M2 catalog derivation, VCR Table 7 discipline)

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.16.2 general format: a constant conditional expression (§2023:7.3.8) — evaluated and diagnosed by the conditional-compilation driver as COBOL1619; >>ELSE and >>END-IF write no operand (checked centrally, §2023:7.3.3 SR3/SR4, as COBOL1911) and the driver's frame stack diagnoses the directive's structure as COBOL2649.

source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725IF.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
       >>IF XX DEFINED
           DISPLAY "Y".
       >>END-IF
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
